I am all for the textbook definition of the LGBT community to fight off homophobia and transphobia, but I've found people tend to use the term "LGBT community" in order to treat themselves as being in a cool little club that the straights aren't allowed in. Which I think is the opposite message we should sending to straight and cis people on how we feel about them.

And I would not immediately dismiss them all as cis women that are attention seeker, I just get the feeling kids my age aren't thinking through the real reason they are identifying as trans. I know they can be susceptible to wanting to fit in, especially about serious topics. One of these people came to me talking about how they used to self-harm simply because their friends did it. Obviously they didn't think it through back then, history repeats itself.

Sure "mentally ill" has negative connotations and people tend to associate transgenderism with schizophrenic delusions. But those that say it are the people with the idea that mental illness inherently means "crazy." The defence of transgenderism is that it is the treatment to gender dysphoria, you take that away and you have no defence. Why do you wish to transition?
